articles.summary: Israeli opposition leader Gadi Eisenkot has moved closer to forming a new government to replace caretaker prime minister Benjamin Netanyahu, securing
articles.body: Israeli opposition leader Gadi Eisenkot has moved closer to forming a new government to replace caretaker prime minister Benjamin Netanyahu, securing coalition agreements with two key political allies as negotiations continue over the parliamentary majority needed to take power.Eisenkot's centrist Yashar party on Thursday reached a coalition agreement with the left-wing Democrats, led by Yair Golan, following a similar deal with the right-wing Yisrael Beiteinu party, headed by former defence minister Avigdor Lieberman, on Tuesday. The developments mark progress in efforts to bring together opposition parties after last month's election failed to give either political bloc a clear majority."Gadi Eisenkot, chair of Yashar with Eisenkot, and Yair Golan, chair of the Democrats, have agreed to sign a coalition agreement between the two parties," a joint statement issued by the parties said on Thursday.The agreement came two days after the Democrats announced they were suspending negotiations with Yashar. Israeli media reports attributed the disagreement to differences over the allocation of ministerial portfolios.Golan called on opposition parties to conclude negotiations and move towards forming a government."We promised the people that we would replace Netanyahu and defend democracy. And that is what we will do. I call on all parties to come together as soon as possible to finalise agreements and sign them, form a government, and lead Israel in a new direction," he said on Thursday."This is the mission of our lives," Golan added.Eisenkot faces challenge of securing parliamentary majorityDespite the agreements, Eisenkot's coalition-building efforts remain incomplete. Yashar, Yisrael Beiteinu and the Democrats together account for 36 lawmakers in Israel's 120-member Knesset, falling well short of the 61 seats required for a parliamentary majority.The bloc also includes Be'Yachad, led by former prime minister Naftali Bennett, which has 12 seats but has yet to sign a formal coalition agreement with Eisenkot. Bennett has indicated that he wants to allow further negotiations with Netanyahu's Likud party over the possibility of a national unity government.According to the Financial Times, negotiations with the ultra-Orthodox United Torah Judaism (UTJ) party have emerged as a crucial part of Eisenkot's efforts to secure a majority. Opposition politicians have reportedly indicated a willingness to reconsider their campaign position on compulsory military service for ultra-Orthodox men to attract the party.The question of cooperation with Arab-majority parties has also exposed divisions within the opposition. While the Democrats have backed support from two Arab-majority lists, Lieberman has opposed relying on Arab parties and favours an arrangement with ultra-Orthodox factions.Lieberman on Thursday accused Netanyahu of attempting to delay the formation of an alternative government."He will drag out negotiations over a 'unity' government until the last moment, look for a pretext to blow them up, and even if such a government is formed, he will try to engineer a crisis within a few months to drag Israel back to elections," he said.Israeli president Isaac Herzog has given Eisenkot until December 6 to form a government, with a possible 14-day extension. The coming days will be crucial as negotiations with Bennett, UTJ and other potential coalition partners continue. Unless Eisenkot secures the required support, Israel could face another round of political uncertainty.You use AI every day. Now get your AI Quotient. Take the AIQ test.

articles.title: Greater Noida man allotted plot in 2006, took possession in 2010 but never moved in; GNIDA raised Rs 14,128 water bill in 2015 for charges since 2011, followed by Rs 19,189 demand despite payment; consumer commission orders Rs 50,000 compensation
articles.summary: NOIDA: A consumer who had not moved into his Greater Noida plot was billed for water over four years, despite claiming he had never used the supply.
articles.body: NOIDA: A consumer who had not moved into his Greater Noida plot was billed for water over four years, despite claiming he had never used the supply. The Greater Noida Industrial Development Authority (GNIDA) continued to raise demands based on fixed monthly charges, eventually prompting him to approach a consumer commission. The Delhi consumer commission has now held the authority guilty of unfair trade practice and directed it to pay Rs 50,000 compensation to the plot owner for the harassment caused. It has also ordered GNIDA to calculate his future bills according to actual water consumption and put in place a mechanism to differentiate between regular users and consumers who do not use their connections.The case dates back to a plot allotted to the complainant in December 2006. He took possession in November 2010 but said he chose not to occupy it because the locality was sparsely inhabited. Despite this, the authority began charging him for water from February 2011. Its first bill, issued in July 2015, sought Rs 14,128, including interest at 12% per annum, for the period up to July 1, 2015. The complainant received it on August 22 that year.He questioned how the authority could demand payment for a service he had not used, particularly when no bills had been issued to him during the earlier years. He also argued that the retrospective demand was time-barred. The complainant's grievance did not end with the first payment. After depositing Rs 14,130 in 2015, he received another bill for Rs 19,189, dated January 7, 2016. Delivered to him on July 2 that year, it covered water charges from 2011 to 2016, along with interest. He alleged that the amount already paid had not been adjusted.Even his attempts to get the connection disconnected failed to stop the demands. He said he sent requests to the authority in July 2016 and March 2019, but received another bill for Rs 34,193 in June 2020. He subsequently challenged the authority's practice of imposing a fixed monthly charge regardless of consumption, arguing that water bills should reflect actual usage. He accused GNIDA of unfair trade practice and sought a refund of the excess charges.GNIDA told the commission that it was a government undertaking operating under rules, regulations and bylaws in the public interest. It said water tariffs were revised every year and that plots measuring less than 250 square metres were charged Rs 150 per month until May 2013. The complainant, it said, had been billed at the prescribed rate. The authority also claimed that Rs 43,167 was outstanding against the plot owner towards water charges up to March 31, 2021. It alleged that he had not paid any amount towards these charges since 2015.The commission noted that the authority had raised its first bill five years after the complainant took possession of the property. It also recorded that he had paid Rs 14,130 against the initial demand in 2015. The commission questioned the rationale behind charging consumers the same amount without determining whether they actually used the water supply. It observed that the authority had no system to establish individual consumption, placing households that used water regularly on the same footing as those that did not use it or accessed it only occasionally.Relying on Supreme Court judgments, the commission said water charges had to be linked to actual consumption and could not be imposed as a fixed levy in the manner of a tax. It concluded that GNIDA's practice of raising bills without taking actual usage into account amounted to unfair trade practice. Besides awarding Rs 50,000 compensation to the complainant, the commission directed the authority to develop a system to identify actual water users and distinguish them from consumers who merely had a connection. articles.title: 'Only winter will come': Bangladesh minister doubts Hasina will return in December
articles.summary: Bangladesh's state minister for foreign affairs on Thursday expressed doubt over the possibility of former PM Sheikh Hasina returning to the country in
articles.body: Bangladesh's state minister for foreign affairs on Thursday expressed doubt over the possibility of former PM Sheikh Hasina returning to the country in December this year. He sarcastically said that "only winter, and not the ousted leader, would arrive," news agency IANS reported.Tarique Rahman's aide reiterated that Hasina could return only through the extradition process under the existing treaty with India."I have already said at a meeting in Sylhet that Sheikh Hasina will not come in December……nobody will come in December; only winter will come,” United News of Bangladesh (UNB) quoted Kobir as saying.Kobir made the remarks while speaking to reporters at the ministry of foreign affairs in Dhaka.He said Bangladesh had already approached the relevant authorities in India seeking Hasina's handover under the extradition treaty.Bangladesh minister maintained that Hasina would have to be brought back in handcuffs or under strict surveillance to face trial, pointing out this as the only route for her return. He added that the request also covered other individuals accused of committing crimes in Bangladesh, UNB reported.The remarks come amid reports that Hasina, who has been living in exile in India, wishes to return to Dhaka aboard a state aircraft on December 16, coinciding with Bangladesh's Victory Day, which marks the country's liberation from Pakistan.Kobir had made a similar statement on Tuesday while responding to questions from journalists after briefing foreign diplomats in Dhaka. Rejecting reports about Hasina's proposed return, he said she could come back only as a prisoner to face justice."This news may be shown and shown by paying money. But we have to distinguish between reality and desire. The reality is that terrorists will be brought back to the country only to face justice. Some may have a wish, some may have nightmares while lying in their bedroom, that they are coming to the airport, boarding a train. But they are not ordinary passengers. They can only be brought back to the country in handcuffs or to face justice. That is the point,” Bangladesh's leading Bengali daily Prothom Alo quoted Kobir as saying.Earlier this month, Hasina asserted that the possibility of arrest, imprisonment or even death would not stop her from returning to Bangladesh. She said she would rather die in her homeland than remain away from her people.In a rare audio interview with news agency IANS, Hasina said she was aware of the risks but had never allowed fear to dictate her decisions. Recalling her previous returns to Bangladesh amid political uncertainty, she said she had faced imprisonment and repeated attempts on her life.“Look, I understand the risks very well. I may be arrested the moment I arrive. They may send me to prison. They may even try to kill me. I have considered all these possibilities. But, you know, I stopped worrying about my personal safety a long time ago. I returned to Bangladesh in 1981, despite military rule. I returned again in 2007, knowing that the military-backed government might arrest me. I have faced imprisonment and repeated attempts on my life. Fear has never stopped me from doing what I believe is right,” she said.Hasina has also reportedly sought a government aircraft to fly her back to Bangladesh.You use AI every day. articles.title: Watch: Putin hails PM Modi's 'Make in India' vision, praises 16-year-old Indian AI entrepreneur
articles.summary: Russian President Vladimir Putin on Thursday praised the work of 16-year-old Indian entrepreneur Raul John Aju, linking his efforts in artificial
articles.body: Russian President Vladimir Putin on Thursday praised the work of 16-year-old Indian entrepreneur Raul John Aju, linking his efforts in artificial intelligence (AI) to Prime Minister Narendra Modi's 'Make in India' initiative during the AI Journey 2026 conference.Putin and Kazakh President Kassym-Jomart Tokayev interacted with young innovators at the conference, where Aju, the founder and chief technology officer (CTO) of AI Realm Technologies, was among those introduced to the Russian president.During the interaction, Putin acknowledged Aju's work and highlighted how young innovators developing their own technological solutions contribute to the objectives of the 'Make in India' initiative."Ultimately your work helps realize PM Modi's "Make in India" call right? Because it helps young people find their own solutions and implement these solutions," Putin told Aju.Putin's remarks come days after the Office of the United States Trade Representative (USTR) criticised India's manufacturing and export policies, including the 'Make in India' initiative, in a report examining structural excess capacity and production in manufacturing sectors.Putin's praise comes days after US trade body targets 'Make in India'In its Section 301 investigation report into India's acts, policies and practices relating to structural excess capacity and production in manufacturing sectors, the USTR alleged that India had adopted several measures that contributed to excess manufacturing capacity and production while failing to effectively address the resulting global concerns."India engages in a range of acts, policies, and practices that create, maintain, or contribute to the structural excess capacity and production evident in the indicia described above. Key among these are the umbrella efforts of Make in India, PLI, Atmanirbhar Bharat (Self-Reliant India), and IBEF, with a particular emphasis on efforts related to or under these efforts in the steel, solar, health, and ICT sectors," the USTR said.The report specifically identified the government's flagship 'Make in India' programme, Production-Linked Incentive (PLI) scheme, Atmanirbhar Bharat initiative and India Brand Equity Foundation (IBEF) among the measures it said contributed to structural excess capacity.Who is Raul John Aju, the 'AI Kid of India'?Popularly known online as 'Raul the Rockstar' and often described as the 'AI Kid of India', Aju is a teenager from Kerala who has pursued artificial intelligence despite coming from a Commerce background rather than a conventional engineering or computer science pathway.According to information shared on his LinkedIn profile, his interest in technology began when he was around nine years old. What started as independent learning and experimentation gradually developed into AI projects, educational initiatives and a growing online community.Aju studied Plus Two Commerce at North Edappally GHSS while simultaneously working on artificial intelligence projects. His LinkedIn profile identifies him as the founder and CTO of AIRealm Technologies, where he develops AI products and practical technology solutions.Projects associated with him include ThinkCraft, RESQ AI and MeBot, among other AI-based tools. He is also associated with ThinkCraft Academy, an AI learning platform that introduces students and professionals to emerging technologies.Beyond developing software, Aju has conducted AI workshops and sessions for students, educators and professionals, with a focus on making the technology accessible to people without technical backgrounds."I build things with AI. I talk about them. Sometimes I break them. Then I build them again," he writes in his LinkedIn introduction.His profile also states that he has delivered eight TEDx talks and conducted sessions at IITs, universities, schools and other institutions. He has built an online following of more than 500,000 people, sharing content related to artificial intelligence and emerging technologies.Get the latest India News and Live updates. articles.title: Gwalior man undergoes prostate cancer treatment in Delhi, Star Health rejects Rs 26,803 claim over OPD care; consumer commission orders Rs 26,803 payout with Rs 3,500 compensation
articles.summary: BHOPAL: A 68-year-old Gwalior man’s Rs 26,803 health insurance claim for prostate cancer treatment has been allowed by the district consumer commission,
articles.body: BHOPAL: A 68-year-old Gwalior man’s Rs 26,803 health insurance claim for prostate cancer treatment has been allowed by the district consumer commission, which held Star Health and Allied Insurance Company guilty of deficiency in service for rejecting it on the ground that the treatment was taken on an outpatient basis.In an order dated November 5, the Gwalior District Consumer Disputes Redressal Commission directed the insurer to pay Brijmohan Shrivastav Rs 26,803 within 45 days. It also ordered the company to pay Rs 2,000 as compensation for mental agony and Rs 1,500 towards litigation expenses.Shrivastav had approached the commission after the insurer rejected his claim for expenses incurred during treatment at Rajiv Gandhi Cancer Institute in Delhi. He said he was undergoing treatment for prostate cancer and submitted a claim of Rs 26,803 after medical examinations and treatment.The insurer rejected the claim, saying Shrivastav had not been admitted to hospital and had received outpatient treatment. It argued that the policy covered only eligible inpatient treatment expenses and that outpatient treatment was not payable.The company also contended that each claim had to be assessed on its own merits and that settlement of earlier claims did not automatically entitle the policyholder to reimbursement.However, the commission noted that the insurer had not specifically disputed Shrivastav’s claim that it had earlier paid claims relating to day-care treatment under the same policy. It also failed to draw the commission’s attention to any specific policy condition that justified rejecting the present claim.Holding that the insurer had failed to establish a valid basis for repudiation, the commission set aside the rejection and directed payment of the claimed amount.The order said that if the insurer failed to pay within 45 days, it would have to pay 6% annual interest on the amount from the expiry of the stipulated period until actual payment.The order was passed by commission president Rajendra Prasad Sharma and member Revati Raman Mishra.You Can Also Check: Gold Rate in Bhopal | Silver Rate in Bhopal | Bank Holidays in Bhopal | Public Holidays in Bhopal | Petrol Price in Bhopal | Diesel Price in Bhopal | CNG Price in Bhopal | LPG Price in BhopalStay updated with the latest Bhopal news. articles.title: 'Fake news': CJP's Ranka threatens legal action over claim leaders fled Nagpur rally venue after Look Out Circulars issued
articles.summary: NEW DELHI: Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) co-convenor Ashutosh Ranka has threatened legal action against news agency IANS, accusing it of spreading fake news
articles.body: NEW DELHI: Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) co-convenor Ashutosh Ranka has threatened legal action against news agency IANS, accusing it of spreading fake news over a video posted on X. The agency had claimed that CJP founder Abhijeet Dipke and his associates left a venue after receiving information about a Look Out Circular (LOC), while avoiding media cameras.In its post, IANS wrote: "As soon as they received information about the Look Out Notice, CJP Founder Abhijeet Dipke and his associates began leaving the spot while avoiding media cameras. They left before Actor Prakash Raj could speak."Responding to the post, Ranka said the agency had published an inaccurate account of the events and warned it to expect a legal notice."Dear IANS, Instead of posting from the IT cell account, you accidentally posted from your official id. You might now wait for a legal notice for spreading fake news, since there are videos of Prakash Sir addressing the audience and all of us comfortably leaving the venue with police around," he wrote on X.The video posted by IANS showed reporters following vehicles carrying CJP leaders as they left the venue. It later showed actor Prakash Raj being escorted by a police official as media personnel gathered around him. However, the footage does not establish the context claimed in the agency's post.The exchange came amid a protest organised by the CJP in Nagpur on Thursday, where Dipke and other party leaders addressed a rally titled 'Save Democracy, Save Constitution' at Samvidhan Chowk on Constitution Day.Addressing the gathering, Dipke accused the BJP-led Centre of undermining the Constitution and alleged that institutions across the country had been hijacked."The government is acting against the Constitution. Not a single institution is left that has not been hijacked," he said.Referring to the LOC issued against him by Mumbai Police, Dipke challenged the authorities to arrest him."There is a lookout notice against me by the Mumbai Police. There is police bandobast here and they are looking for me. Where is Abhijeet Dipke? I am here in Samvidhan Chowk. What will you do? Arrest me. I have been in jail twice. Don't show me the fear of jail," he said.Ranka, meanwhile, said the party was preparing to expand its activities beyond protests in major cities. "We will go to every village, interact with people and give a voice to the youth," he said.Mumbai Police have issued LOCs against Dipke, Ranka and CJP leader Saurav Das in connection with an FIR over an alleged unauthorised protest at Shivaji Park on Gandhi Jayanti. Police said the circulars were issued to prevent the leaders from leaving the country while the investigation was underway.Das was stopped at the airport on November 23 while attempting to travel to the United Kingdom for an event at Oxford University. He has challenged the LOC before the Delhi High Court.Get the latest India News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: Bengaluru man pays Rs 2 lakh to book residential plot, cancels deal over missing legal documents; builder fails to refund despite written assurance, consumer commission orders Rs 2 lakh refund with 9% interest and Rs 25,000 compensation
articles.summary: BENGALURU: A Bengaluru consumer commission has directed a real estate company and its two directors to refund Rs 2 lakh to a 41-year-old man who cancelled
articles.body: BENGALURU: A Bengaluru consumer commission has directed a real estate company and its two directors to refund Rs 2 lakh to a 41-year-old man who cancelled the booking of a residential plot after the builder allegedly failed to provide essential property documents. The commission also ordered them to pay Rs 25,000 towards compensation and litigation expenses.The District Consumer Disputes Redressal Commission (Bengaluru Urban), in an order dated October 7, directed Virtue Infra Builders Pvt Ltd and its directors, R M Harikrishna and Aravinda Kumar, to refund the booking amount with 9% annual interest from July 19, 2024, until payment.The commission also ordered the opposite parties to pay Rs 10,000 for deficiency in service, Rs 10,000 for pain and suffering, and Rs 5,000 towards litigation costs. They have been given 45 days to comply with the order.According to the complaint filed by Muni Rao, he had approached the company to purchase a residential plot in its Virtue Star City project at Mathkur village in Bengaluru North. Based on the company's representations about the property's title, approvals and availability for immediate registration, he agreed to purchase plot No. 66, measuring 1,410 sq ft.On July 19, 2024, Rao paid Rs 2 lakh as advance booking amount, comprising Rs 1.5 lakh through cheque and Rs 50,000 through an online transaction.However, after receiving the payment, the company allegedly failed to provide the complete legal documents required to verify the title and legality of the transaction. These included mother deeds and title documents, land conversion order, approved layout plan, RERA approval and e-Khata documents.Unable to verify the property's legal status, Rao decided to cancel the booking and sought a refund. Despite repeated requests, phone calls and emails, the company did not return the money, according to the complaint.On August 21, 2024, the company acknowledged its liability to refund the booking amount through an email and assured Rao that the money would be credited by November 20, 2024. It also apologised for the delay and assured him that the refund would be processed. However, the payment was not made even after the promised deadline, forcing him to approach the consumer commission.The commission noted that the builder and its directors failed to appear before it despite receiving notice and did not file their written version. The matter was consequently heard ex parte.After examining the complainant's affidavit and supporting documents, the commission observed that the company had failed to furnish the necessary property documents despite receiving the advance amount. It also noted that the company had acknowledged its liability to refund the money but had failed to honour its assurance.The commission held the company and its two directors jointly and severally liable, observing that the complainant was neither given possession of the plot nor refunded the deposited amount. articles.title: 'BJP's biggest political mistake': Akhilesh slams Delimitation Bill ahead of Parliament's special session - How numbers stack up
articles.summary: NEW DELHI: Samajwadi Party chief Akhilesh Yadav on Friday attacked the ruling BJP over the proposed delimitation-linked women's reservation bill, saying
articles.body: NEW DELHI: Samajwadi Party chief Akhilesh Yadav on Friday attacked the ruling BJP over the proposed delimitation-linked women's reservation bill, saying it would prove to be the party's “biggest political mistake”.“Delimitation will prove to be the biggest political mistake made by the BJP,” Akhilesh said in a post on X.His remarks came a day after the government announced a special sitting of Parliament from November 30 to December 3 to transact “essential” business, amid speculation that it may reintroduce the delimitation-linked women's reservation bill.The proposed legislation seeks to increase the Lok Sabha's strength from 543 to a maximum of 850 seats through delimitation, paving the way for the implementation of 33% reservation for women in Parliament and state legislatures ahead of the 2029 general elections.‘Mischievous PM-HM jodi is lying’Congress also alleged that the special session had little to do with women's reservation and accused the government of using it to push the delimitation bill.“Yet again, the mischievous PM-HM jodi is lying,” Congress general secretary Jairam Ramesh said on X.Ramesh pointed out that the Nari Shakti Vandan Adhiniyam, providing one-third reservation for women, was passed unanimously by Parliament in September 2023.The Congress president had subsequently demanded its immediate implementation, but the law was not notified until 10.40 pm on April 16, 2026, he said.“The Special Session is thus NOT for women's reservation. That is already a law which the PM-HM jodi have put into cold storage for over three years,” Ramesh said.He alleged that the government was convening Parliament to push delimitation and redraw constituencies to benefit the BJP.“And who will be in charge of deciding the geography of constituencies? It will be a thoroughly compromised and brutally exposed CEC, Gyanesh Kumar, who has made a complete mockery of preparation of electoral rolls and destroyed the integrity of the electoral process,” he said.“The executors of Vote Chori on such a gigantic scale are to be given the powers to carry out delimitation and manipulate the nature of constituencies. This is as atrocious as you can get.“This is a desperate move by a nervous and rattled PM who is under siege. It will be countered with firm resolve,” Ramesh added.The Congress has also alleged that the government is hoping to secure a “super-tainted” two-thirds majority to pass the Constitution amendment bill.‘Thackeray is no more, Pawar is unwell’: Shiv Sena (UBT)Shiv Sena (UBT) leader Sanjay Raut also opposed the proposed delimitation exercise, alleging that it was a BJP conspiracy to take away people's political power.Sharing a post on X, Raut said, “Today, Shiv Sena chief Balasaheb Thackeray is no longer with us: Sharad Pawar is unwell and in no position to fight or make decisions, otherwise the anti-national Delimitation Bill would never have dared to be brought before Parliament in such a corrupt manner: Delimitation is a BJP conspiracy to strip the people of this country of their power.”“Anyone who supports it is betraying the people of this country… They will be known as the biggest traitors of the 21st century! Therefore, every patriotic, democratic party should reject Delimitation in Parliament. History always remembers the names of traitors; Explanations for betrayal fade into thin air” he added.Meanwhile, the YSR Congress Party (YSRCP) is likely to support the delimitation bill, provided it ensures regional balance, party sources told ANI.Decoding delimitation mathsThe Lok Sabha Secretariat said the second part of the eighth session of the 18th Lok Sabha will begin on November 30. The special sitting is expected to conclude on December 3, subject to the exigencies of government business.The sittings will be an extension of the Monsoon Session, which was adjourned sine die on August 13 but not prorogued.Earlier on Thursday, Union parliamentary affairs minister Kiren Rijiju said the government had requested the Lok Sabha Speaker and Rajya Sabha Chairman to reconvene the Houses to transact essential government business.The Union Cabinet is also scheduled to meet on Friday and is likely to discuss the delimitation-linked women's reservation legislation, sources said.The developments follow Prime Minister Narendra Modi's remarks on Thursday, accusing an opposition party of blocking the Constitution (131st Amendment) Bill, 2026, in April.In a signed article published in newspapers, PM Modi, “The journey of our Constitution would be incomplete without recognising the remarkable women who helped shape it. But what happened earlier this year should fill our hearts with shame.”“I assure the 'Nari Shakti' of India that no force can prevent us from ensuring that justice is done to them,” he added.The bill was defeated in April after the government failed to secure the required two-thirds majority in the Lok Sabha. It needs 361 votes in the 543-member House, which currently has 540 members due to three vacancies.The NDA has around 320 MPs and would require additional support from opposition parties to cross the threshold.The government's position has strengthened since the bill's defeat in April, with 26 MPs moving out of the opposition camp.Twenty rebel Trinamool Congress MPs broke away and merged with the Nationalist Citizens Party of India (NCPI), pledging support to the NDA, while six Shiv Sena (UBT) MPs joined the Eknath Shinde-led Shiv Sena.However, the ruling alliance still needs additional votes. The DMK, with 22 Lok Sabha MPs, and the NCP (SP), with eight, could play a significant role in the evolving political arithmetic.Opposition parties are also expected to raise their protests against the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls and demand the resignation of Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar, potentially leading to another stormy session.Get the latest India News and Live updates. articles.title: 'Don't waste court's time': SC declines urgent hearing on plea against Ranbir's Ramayana
articles.summary: NEW DELHI: The Supreme Court on Friday declined to grant an urgent hearing to a petition challenging the release of Ranbir Kapoor-starrer Ramayana: Rise
articles.body: NEW DELHI: The Supreme Court on Friday declined to grant an urgent hearing to a petition challenging the release of Ranbir Kapoor-starrer Ramayana: Rise of a Legend, observing that those who disagree with the film's interpretation of the epic are free to make a film presenting their own perspective.A bench comprising Chief Justice Surya Kant and Justices Joymalya Bagchi and V Mohana questioned the urgency of the plea, noting that the film had already been released in theatres and that those interested in watching it had already done so.The petitioner's counsel told the bench that the plea had been registered on November 23 but was yet to be listed for hearing."The movie has already been released. Those who wanted to watch it have already seen it," the CJI said.The counsel argued that "many facts have been distorted" in the film's depiction of the epic. Responding to this, Justice Bagchi said, "They made a movie as they understand, you make a movie as you understand. Don't waste the time of the court."The CJI also remarked, "If you have a counter-view about the epic, you make a movie on the counter-view. Don't waste time of the Court."As the counsel pressed for an early hearing, the bench said the matter would be listed in due course.The petition alleges that the filmmakers distorted mythological facts in their portrayal of the Ramayana.Ramayana: Rise of a Legend, also referred to as Ramayana: Part 1, is directed by Nitesh Tiwari and produced by Namit Malhotra. The film features Ranbir Kapoor as Lord Rama, Sai Pallavi as Sita and Yash as Ravana. Its ensemble cast includes Sunny Deol, Ravie Dubey, Lara Dutta, Arun Govil, Kajal Aggarwal, Rakul Preet Singh and Vivek Oberoi.The film was released in theatres on November 5, 2026.Get the latest India News and Live updates. articles.title: More than 60 years after 114 late Roman silver coins were found during road widening in Kent, the first part of the Springhead Hoard sold for £23,240, with proceeds supporting a century-old local history group
articles.summary: A collection of 114 silver coins buried during the late Roman period and discovered during road construction in Kent more than six decades ago has sold
articles.body: A collection of 114 silver coins buried during the late Roman period and discovered during road construction in Kent more than six decades ago has sold for £23,240 at auction. The money will help preserve the archives of the local historical society whose members played a major role in recovering the ancient treasure.The coins formed the first part of the Springhead Hoard, discovered on October 22, 1964, when workers were widening the A2 road near Springhead in Kent, England. Members of the Gravesend Historical Society joined the recovery effort after the hoard was uncovered.According to the official website of auction house Noonans, the 114 silver coins, known as ‘siliquae,’ were sold on November 10, 2026. All the coins found buyers, and the sale exceeded the auction's highest estimate of £15,000. The remaining coins owned by the society are scheduled to be offered in spring 2027.The proceeds will support the society, which was founded in 1924 and recently marked its centenary. The money will be used to store, conserve and digitise its research archive, including photographs, documents, excavation records and artefacts from the Roman site.Coins remained buried for around 1,600 yearsThe Springhead Hoard is believed to have been buried around AD 388, during a period of political unrest, raids and rebellion in the late Roman Empire. The coins were struck under several Roman emperors, spanning the reigns of Constantius II to Magnus Maximus.They remained underground for approximately 1,600 years before road-widening work brought them to light. The discovery took place at Springhead, the site of the Roman settlement known as Vagniacis. According to Richard Taylor, honorary secretary of the Gravesend Historical Society, the organisation had been excavating the area since the 1950s. Its members had uncovered remains of temples, shops and roads at the settlement, which stood along the Roman route known as Watling Street.In a pre-auction account published by Noonans, Taylor said travellers using the road may have stopped at the religious centre to pray for healing and good fortune. The excavation became particularly important after the hoard was found. A total of 447 coins were recovered, with the historical society's members contributing significantly to the search.Volunteers searched on their knees as roadworks continuedVictor Smith, one of the original excavators, was among the society members who helped recover the coins. He attended the November 10 auction, more than six decades after the discovery. Recalling the recovery work in an earlier statement published by Noonans, Smith described how members searched on their knees, moving along parallel lines separated by strings while heavy earth-moving machinery continued working nearby.In January 1965, an inquest at Northfleet Town Hall declared the hoard Treasure Trove. The British Museum took 27 coins, including the gold pieces. The Gravesend Historical Society acquired the remaining 420 silver siliquae using its reward, supplemented by money from its museum fund.Some coins sold for several times their estimatesThe first auction included coins from several Roman emperors, with some attracting bids well above their estimates. According to Noonans, a silver siliqua from the reign of Gratian (367–383), minted in Trier between 367 and 378, sold for a hammer price of £440 against an estimate of £100–£150. One side showed a draped bust, while the other depicted Roma seated on a throne.A coin from the reign of Magnus Maximus (383–388), also minted in Trier, fetched £420 against an estimate of £100–£150. Another from the reign of Theodosius I (379–395) sold for £400. A coin from the reign of Valentinian II (375–392), minted at Aquileia in north-eastern Italy, achieved £380.Noonans' auction report records a gross sale total of £23,240, rising to £28,818 when the buyers' premium is included.Sale proceeds to preserve Gravesend's local historyThe society plans to retain a small representative group of coins, including examples from each emperor represented in the hoard. These will remain in Gravesend as a permanent reminder of the discovery.The money raised from the sale will help the organisation preserve and make its historical archive more accessible to residents, schools and researchers. The remaining coins from the society's collection are expected to be auctioned in spring 2027, continuing a sale that began with the first 114 pieces.You use AI every day. Now get your AI Quotient. articles.title: DMK 'ready' to support BJP's delimitation bill if Tamil Nadu's representation remains unchanged
articles.summary: CHENNAI: DMK is ready to support the BJP-led Union govt’s proposed delimitation bill if it maintains Tamil Nadu’s existing percentage of representation
articles.body: CHENNAI: DMK is ready to support the BJP-led Union govt’s proposed delimitation bill if it maintains Tamil Nadu’s existing percentage of representation and includes a provision for a 25-year freeze, party sources told TOI.It is reliably learned that DMK leadership placed these two demands before the BJP when the latter recently reached out to the Dravidian party.Asked if the party would support a 50% increase in the number of seats across all states from the current strength, a senior DMK leader said, “Yes, with provision built in the bill for a 25-year freeze and maintaining existing representation from all states. Had we not opposed the bill in the past, we could have lost this proposition. If BJP is ready to incorporate these two demands, we have nothing to lose but to gain more in future.”DMK had opposed delimitation because Tamil Nadu’s representation could be reduced if the 2027 census was used as the basis for the exercise, sources said.“If the new draft bill ensures Tamil Nadu will continue to have the same percentage representation and next delimitation based on the latest census will be carried out only after 25 years, not 100 years as suggested by few, it is a fair deal. It will be beneficial for both DMK as well as Tamil Nadu,” a source said.Asked whether the BJP had recently reached out to DMK, the source said, “Yes, they did and we have given them the demands.”DMK has 22 MPs in Lok Sabha and 8 MPs in Rajya Sabha. The party has maintained that it is not opposed to delimitation but wants the process to be fair to all sides. In August, DMK backed a resolution of the TVK govt in the assembly urging the Union govt to freeze the current strength of the Lok Sabha at 543 seats.DMK chief and former Tamil Nadu chief minister, MK Stalin, in a post on X, said, “If the number of parliamentary constituencies is increased, under no circumstances should Tamil Nadu’s share fall below its current 7.18%! The existing proportion of parliamentary representation among States, as determined on the basis of the 1971 Census and frozen earlier, must remain unchanged for another 25 years!”“The DMK remains firm on both these positions today and will continue to do so. The speculation being spread in the media and the grumbling of backstabbers will not shake our position in any way. The DMK will never compromise on Tamil Nadu’s interests,” he added.Meanwhile, CPM state secretary Shanmugam expressed concern over reports that the Union govt had “reached an understanding” with the DMK on the delimitation bill. “On behalf of the CPM, we urge the DMK to remain steadfast in its commitment to protecting the interests of Tamil Nadu and the southern states,” he posted on X.Shanmugam urged the DMK leadership to clarify its stance on delimitation without leaving room for speculation.You Can Also Check: Gold Rate in Chennai | Silver Rate in Chennai | Bank Holidays in Chennai | Public Holidays in Chennai | Chennai AQI | Weather in Chennai | Petrol Price in Chennai | Diesel Price in Chennai | CNG Price in Chennai | LPG Price in ChennaiStay updated with the latest Chennai news. articles.title: A Brisbane buyer agreed to pay $4.2 million for two luxury apartments, but the developer cancelled the deal and resold them for $8.8 million; an appeals court overturned an approximately $6.1 million compensation award
articles.summary: A Brisbane buyer contracted in June 2017 to purchase two sub-penthouses in the Luminare building at Newstead for $4,200,000, before construction of the
articles.body: A Brisbane buyer contracted in June 2017 to purchase two sub-penthouses in the Luminare building at Newstead for $4,200,000, before construction of the building had begun. On 13 April 2023, the developer gave notice ending the contract. It later sold the lots for $3,500,000 and $5,300,000. At trial, Bowskill CJ found the termination unlawful, invalid and of no effect, and judgment was ordered for $6,097,841.42, including interest. On 30 October 2026, the Court of Appeal, by majority, allowed the developer's appeal, set aside that judgment and dismissed the buyer's claim, apart from a declaration that the buyer is entitled to the deposit, with the buyer to pay the developer's costs of the claim and the appeal.How a $4.2 million Brisbane apartment deal ended in courtAccording to the Supreme Court of Queensland judgment, it was not disputed that each of the separate title requirements had been met by 14 November 2022, nor that the defendant became aware of this at around that time. The Court of Appeal's reasons record that the plan was registered, the community management statement recorded and the scheme established on or about 28 October 2022, and that separate titles were issued on or about 14 November 2022. The developer did not give the clause 8.1 notice. On 13 April 2023, its solicitor wrote to the buyer's then solicitor giving notice ending the contract under clause 8.3. The letter stated that the seller was not able to give a certificate of occupancy to provide vacant possession by the sunset date, and that the deposit would be refunded. A director of the defendant, Mr Cavallucci, gave evidence that at the time of the letter he estimated both lots to be less than 50 per cent complete. The judgment records that a certificate of occupancy was not issued for either lot until 20 January 2024.The buyer's solicitor responded on 20 June 2023, refusing to accept the purported termination. The reasons record no further correspondence until 22 March 2024, when the defendant's solicitors asked for bank account details to refund the deposit. Ms Jiang, the director of the plaintiff, said that after seeing that letter she became seriously concerned and sought legal advice, and in doing so learned that the defendant had already sold lot 2404 and had contracted to sell lot 2403. Lot 2404 was sold for $3,500,000 under a contract made on 27 September 2023, and that sale was completed on 13 December 2023. On 1 May 2024, the defendant contracted to sell lot 2403 for $5,300,000, and that sale was completed on 3 July 2024. The reasons also record that on 24 June 2024 the plaintiff lodged a caveat over lot 2403, and that it was removed by order made on 28 June 2024.Buyer secured a $6.1 million compensation awardBowskill CJ identified the issues as whether the termination under clause 8.3 was lawful, whether clause 13.1(c) could justify it, whether the buyer breached the contract by lodging the caveat, and what damages were payable. Her Honour accepted the buyer's construction of clause 8.3. According to the reasons, "cannot" in its ordinary meaning refers to an inability to do a thing, and where the separate title conditions had been met and the seller knew it, the seller was able to give the notice, even though the second sentence of clause 8.1 allowed it to delay. Her Honour found that the purported termination on 13 April 2023 was "unlawful, invalid and of no effect". On clause 13.1(c), which allows the seller to terminate if "at any time" it forms the opinion that clause 8.3 "will apply", her Honour held that the clause contemplates the seller forming that opinion before the date in clause 8.3. She therefore found that the contract remained on foot after 13 April 2023.On the caveat, Bowskill CJ found that clause 23 prohibits a caveat over the "Land" or "any land containing the Lot" but does not prohibit a caveat over the lot itself, so there was no breach and the counterclaim was dismissed. On damages, the parties agreed the measure was the difference between the contract price and the market value of the two lots at the date the contract would have completed but for the repudiation, nominated as 5 February 2024, which the judgment describes as 14 days from the issue of the certificate of occupancy on 20 January 2024. The plaintiff relied on a valuer, Mr Walton. Her Honour accepted his evidence that the market value of lot 2403 was $5,300,000. For lot 2404, she accepted his range of $5,000,000 to $5,500,000 and adopted the lower figure of $5,000,000. She found the combined market value to be $10,300,000 and ordered judgment for the difference between that figure and the $4,200,000 contract price, stated in the reasons as $6,100,000, with the deposit to be accounted for and interest to be awarded under s 58 of the Civil Proceedings Act 2011 (Qld).Why the Queensland Court of Appeal overturned a $6.1 million awardIn CAV Gasworks Pty Ltd v JYP Jiang Pty Ltd [2026] QCA 221, delivered on 30 October 2026 by Bradley JA, Crow J and Hindman J, the Court recorded that the record shows that the trial judgment ordered the seller to pay $6,097,841.42, including $417,841.42 in interest. On 23 June 2025, the Court also ordered the seller to pay the buyer's costs, including indemnity costs from 21 November 2024. The seller appealed on two grounds: that the primary judge erred in finding it did not lawfully terminate under clause 8.3, and that she erred in finding it could not rely on clause 13.1(c) after the sunset date. A third ground challenged the costs order. Bradley JA would have dismissed the appeal. His Honour held that the primary judge's approach was an objective reading of the text of clause 8 in the context of the whole contract, and that the seller had no right to terminate under clause 8.3 on 13 April 2023.Crow J and Hindman J, however, would allow the appeal, each for different reasons. Crow J construed "cannot" in clause 8.3 as "cannot because the seller is unable to meet its obligations in clause 7.4", and concluded that the seller's termination was lawful. Hindman J described the construction issue as "finely balanced" but preferred the seller's construction, holding that the second sentence of clause 8.1 operates as a condition precedent to the obligation to give notice. His Honour's approach rested on an implied term that the seller must act honestly, reasonably and without hindering the purpose of the express conditions. Both judges agreed with the primary judge that clause 13.1(c) operates prospectively, and Hindman J considered it unnecessary to decide the second ground. The Court's orders allow the appeal, set aside paragraph 1 of the orders of 12 June 2025, the first paragraph of the judgment of that date and the whole of the order of 23 June 2025, and dismiss the plaintiff's claim save for the declaration made in the second paragraph of the 2025 judgment. They require the plaintiff to pay the appellant's costs of the claim and the appeal on the standard basis, with no order as to costs on the counterclaim.Disclaimer: This article is based on information contained in publicly available court judgments. The Times of India has not independently verified the property details, purchase price, resale prices or other transaction-related information mentioned. The report is intended for informational purposes and should not be construed as legal advice or an independent verification of the claims and findings discussed in the judgments.You use AI every day. articles.title: Pakistani actor's 2017 selfie with Hafiz Saeed resurfaces amid Netflix series row
articles.summary: A 2017 photograph of Pakistani actor Hamza Abbasi posing for a selfie with Lashkar-e-Taiba (LeT) chief Hafiz Saeed has resurfaced amid the controversy
articles.body: A 2017 photograph of Pakistani actor Hamza Abbasi posing for a selfie with Lashkar-e-Taiba (LeT) chief Hafiz Saeed has resurfaced amid the controversy over the proposed streaming of Pakistani web series 'Jo Bachay Hain Sang Samait Lo' in India. The development comes after the Centre directed Netflix to comply with its May 8, 2025 order barring Pakistani-origin content from being streamed in the country.The Union government's order was issued as a punitive measure following the Pakistan-backed Pahalgam terror attack last year.The series, which features Fawad Khan and Mahira Khan, also has Abbasi in its cast.The resurfaced photograph, reportedly taken in 2017, shows the actor posing alongside Pakistani terrorist Hafiz Saeed, who is wanted in India for his role in several terror attacks, including the 2008 Mumbai attacks.A day earlier, the ministry of information and broadcasting asked Netflix to honour the commitment it made in June last year, when the streaming platform informed the ministry that no film or series originating in Pakistan had been made available to subscribers in India.According to sources quoted by news agency ANI, the ministry has asked the platform to maintain the position it had communicated at the time and ensure that Pakistani-origin content is not streamed in India.The direction followed several complaints and representations received by the ministry over the possible release of 'Jo Bachay Hain Sang Samait Lo' in India.On Wednesday, film industry bodies also urged Prime Minister Narendra Modi and the Centre to intervene and prevent the series from being released in the country.The All Indian Cine Workers Association (AICWA) and the Federation of Western India Cine Employees (FWICE) wrote to the Prime Minister, arguing that the show's release would violate the advisory issued following last year's Pahalgam terror attack.The Pahalgam attack was carried out by The Resistance Front (TRF), an offshoot of Pakistan-based Lashkar-e-Taiba.You use AI every day. articles.title: Florida woman sends $1.8 million of elderly mother's money to man posing as French billionaire; court orders her to pay $5.5 million in brother's lawsuit
articles.summary: A Florida woman who transferred nearly $1.85 million belonging to her elderly mother to unknown recipients at the direction of a man posing as a French
articles.body: A Florida woman who transferred nearly $1.85 million belonging to her elderly mother to unknown recipients at the direction of a man posing as a French billionaire has lost an appeal against a $5.5 million judgment in a lawsuit brought by her brother. Kimberly S. Langston had been acting under a power of attorney when she moved the money from her mother's bank account into her own account before sending it elsewhere. She later told her brother, Michael R. Burrows, that she had been defrauded by the man she met online and had become romantically involved with. On November 25, 2026, Florida's Third District Court of Appeal upheld the trial court's judgment of $5,537,250 against her, finding that the undisputed evidence established exploitation of an elderly person. Florida woman loses her mother's $1.8 millionAccording to the appellate court's November 25 opinion, Langston and Burrows are siblings, and their dispute concerned the handling of their mother Sherry L. Burrows' finances.In June 2013, their mother signed a durable power of attorney naming her husband as her agent and Langston as his successor. At some point, Langston became her mother's agent under the arrangement.In March 2020, Langston emailed her brother informing him that she had been defrauded by a man she met on the internet who claimed to be French billionaire François-Henri Pinault.The court recorded that $1,845,740 belonging to their mother had disappeared. Langston had first transferred the money into her own personal bank account before sending it to unknown individuals at the direction of the online contact.During her deposition, she testified that she had become romantically involved with the man after meeting him online. She acknowledged that she had never met him in person or otherwise verified his identity while transferring her mother's money.What did the online man claim about the $420,000 payment?The court's opinion also highlighted a particularly unusual transaction involving a purported agent of the man claiming to be Pinault.According to the trial court's findings, Langston used her mother's money to arrange a purported $420,000 payment for the release of the man's agent, who was allegedly stopped by US Customs. She was told that the money would be used to secure the agent's release.However, the payment was directed to an unknown person who supposedly would pay the amount to US Customs. The appellate court noted that there was no evidence establishing that the transaction was genuine.Langston also failed to carry out due diligence on the purported investments, obtain receipts or other proof of where the money was going, or verify the identity of the person she was communicating with.The court further noted that she continued transferring money despite receiving no returns from earlier purported investments.Why did her brother take her to court?Michael Burrows filed a lawsuit against his sister over the handling of their mother's money. His claims included exploitation of an elderly person, civil theft, breach of a promissory note and unjust enrichment.He argued that Langston had misused the authority granted to her under the power of attorney by transferring their mother's money into her personal account and subsequently sending it to unknown recipients.The trial court granted Burrows' motion for summary judgment on the claims of elder exploitation and civil theft, awarding him $5,537,250.Langston challenged the decision, arguing that her brother had not provided sufficient admissible evidence to establish that their mother qualified as an elderly person under Florida law. She also disputed whether the evidence established the required intent to prove exploitation.What did the appeals court say about the mother's condition?In its November 25 ruling, the Third District Court of Appeal examined whether Sherry Burrows qualified as an elderly person under Florida's elder-exploitation law.Under the state's legislation, the definition includes a person aged 60 or older whose physical, mental or emotional condition impairs their ability to adequately provide for their own care or protection.The court found that the undisputed evidence established that Sherry was over 60 and had been diagnosed with Alzheimer's disease. It also referred to testimony about her memory problems, including instances when she forgot to take her medication.The judges cited a July 2019 message Langston had sent to the online impersonator in which she mentioned her mother's Alzheimer's diagnosis and described her difficulties.The court also noted that Sherry had wanted to return to Colorado, where she had previously lived, but was unable to do so because of her illness. Based on the evidence, the appeals court concluded that her condition impaired her ability to adequately care for and protect herself.Why did the court uphold the $5.5 million judgment?Langston argued that the evidence did not establish whether she had deliberately exploited her mother or had merely acted negligently.However, the appeals court rejected that argument, explaining that a breach of fiduciary duty under Florida's elder-exploitation law can arise from either negligent or intentional conduct.The judges also observed that an agent acting under a power of attorney cannot simply transfer the principal's property into their own account. By moving her mother's money into her personal account before sending it elsewhere, Langston had abused her authority and breached her fiduciary duties.The court identified several other failures, including her inability to verify the online contact's identity, the absence of due diligence on the purported investments and her continued transfers despite growing doubts about the man's identity.Langston had argued that she verified the man's identity through a video chat. However, the court cited a subsequent message in which she expressed doubts, saying she believed the video might have been a recording of the real François-Henri Pinault rather than a live conversation.The appeals court concluded that the undisputed evidence established multiple grounds for finding that Langston had exploited her mother. It therefore affirmed the trial court's $5,537,250 judgment in Burrows' favour.You use AI every day. Now get your AI Quotient. Take the AIQ test.

articles.title: In 1961, a California father buried a letter beneath the playhouse he built for his daughter; 58 years later, it surfaced decades after his death, and the girl he wrote to was now a grandmother
articles.summary: A heartwarming story of a letter buried by a father in 1961 that was discovered decades later, revealing a family's history and memories cherished over generations.
articles.body: A letter can sit in the dark for decades and still reach the right person. In 1961, a father in Northridge, California, wrote a letter to his daughter and buried it in the family backyard. ABC7 Los Angeles reported it was dated 26 November 1961 and marked the completion of a playhouse built by her father and grandfather. It remained hidden for 58 years until the playhouse was pulled down in 2019. By then, the girl it was written for had grown up, lost her father long ago, and become a grandmother herself.The playhouse that kept a secretThe girl in this story is Jacqueline Louise Bennett, who now goes by Lyn Campbell. She was an only child of her parents and lived in the Northridge house for 27 years. Her father and grandfather built the playhouse, and her father had buried the letter without telling anyone. She lost him when she was eight, and all her memories of him were connected to that house. She said it felt like he was still around her, and she described herself as a “daddy's girl.” Even after she moved away, she came back from time to time to visit her old home and old school.The family that kept the capsuleThe next chapter that began in 2019 was another family's. Grace Medrano and her husband were working on updating their backyard, and the work included tearing down the playhouse. Their contractor then found the time capsule. Medrano didn't toss it away. She thought it must have meant something to somebody and saved it as a small piece of the house's history. After the couple began their own family, she wanted to show it to her daughter as she grew older and tell her that the home once belonged to another little girl. Campbell later said the family didn't know her and had no reason to think that anyone connected with the house would ever turn up. The capsule stayed with the Medranos from 2019 until her visit, a gap of roughly five years.A visit in late 2024Campbell's visit came later in 2024. She got in touch with the current homeowners, and it was during that conversation that she learned about the capsule. She called the moment very emotional and wondered how Medrano was able to keep it. From her point of view, the family could have easily thrown it out. She also pointed out that the discovery was only made possible because the playhouse was torn down. If the playhouse had still been standing, no one would have known the letter was even there. ABC7 described the story as a feel-good holiday tale, more than 60 years in the making, and the capsule as a precious gift.Passing the memories onFor Campbell, the gift wasn't just for her. She showed the capsule to her son and grandson and said she was going to pass it on to them. She hoped that they would carry on her memories of the people and places that mattered most. This detail shapes the narrative. In 1961, a father hid a note for his only child. In 2019, a stranger saved it. Now a grandmother plans to pass it on to her family. In the end, a note buried in 1961 took more than 60 years to reach the little girl it was meant for.You use AI every day. Now get your AI Quotient. Take the AIQ test.

articles.title: In 1911, 12 American grey squirrels arrived in Ireland as a wedding gift from England; by 1999, they occupied 22 of 32 counties, and native reds lost 20% of their range
articles.summary: Explore how a wedding gift of grey squirrels in 1911 led to a dramatic decline in native red squirrel populations in Ireland and learn about the recent resurgence of red squirrels due to the pine marten's comeback.
articles.body: Some wedding gifts get tucked away in a cupboard. Others end up changing a country's wildlife. In 1911, 12 grey squirrels, a species native to North America, were introduced to County Longford, Ireland, as a wedding gift from England. According to a 2000 study published in Mammal Review, surveys carried out between 1994 and 1996 found that the species had reached 22 of the island's 32 counties.A wedding present with big consequencesA document on the South Dublin County Council website explains how the squirrels arrived. It says grey squirrels reached Ireland from Britain in 1911, brought by the Earl of Granard. The 12 animals were gifted during a wedding ceremony at Castle Forbes. This is thought to be a single introduction event. The small group of grey squirrels didn't stay small for very long. Grey squirrels can have ten offspring per year, and at the time, there was no significant predation to hold back their numbers. In just decades, grey squirrels had become common throughout the Midlands, the eastern parts and the northern regions of Ireland. They then went on to displace the native red squirrels through competition and the spread of the squirrelpox virus. That's a lot of change to come from one small group of animals.How far the greys spreadThe Mammal Review study gives a clear snapshot of the 1990s. Between 1994 and 1996, researchers surveyed Northern Ireland and the Republic of Ireland using different methods in each. In Northern Ireland, all suitable habitats of at least 15 hectares were searched for the presence or absence of each species. In the Republic, data came from questionnaires given to government and independent wildlife bodies. The results together showed greys in 22 of the 32 counties and described the species as more widespread than before. Red squirrels were still widespread and locally common and found in all but two counties. The rate of spread of the greys varied from none to an estimated 13.4 km a year. Geographical features, mostly rivers, slowed them down in some directions.Why red squirrels lost groundThe council’s FAQ notes that greys have several advantages over reds. First, they are bigger than the reds. They can digest seeds and acorns even before they ripen, unlike the reds. Grey squirrels also carry squirrelpox virus. This virus doesn't cause any symptoms in the greys, but it is fatal for the reds. It can devastate local red populations within weeks. The FAQ indicates that the introduction of grey squirrels in Ireland led to a significant decrease in the number of native red squirrels in the country. By 2009, the red squirrel’s range had declined by 20% and was considered threatened with extinction. A few years later, the last populations in suburban Dublin, at Killiney and Howth, went extinct.Signs of a comebackThe story doesn't end there. The council also reports that the range of the grey squirrel in Ireland has declined significantly over the last two decades, as the predator pine marten has made a comeback. This is supported by the All-Ireland Squirrel and Pine Marten Survey 2019, a citizen science project led by what was then NUI Galway and published by the National Parks and Wildlife Service in 2020. It found that greys had disappeared from parts of the Midlands. Pine martens were found at high densities in those areas, and in many of them red squirrels were recovering. However, pine martens rarely use urban areas and are not expected to suppress greys in cities such as Dublin. So the story that began with those 12 squirrels is still being written.You use AI every day. Now get your AI Quotient. Take the AIQ test.

articles.title: 'US F-16 forced to retreat’: Iran claims warning shots drove fighter jet away from its airspace
articles.summary: Iran's Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC) on Friday claimed that its air defence systems fired warning shots at a US F-16 fighter jet near Hengam
articles.body: Iran's Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC) on Friday claimed that its air defence systems fired warning shots at a US F-16 fighter jet near Hengam Island in the Strait of Hormuz.
